import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated group which is not nilpotent-by-finite and whose
growth function has as a majorant a function of the form $c^{\sqrt{n}}$, where $c$ is a
constant greater than $1$?

A negative answer is Grigorchuk's gap conjecture, see
`FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/GapConjecture.lean`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.9»

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated group which is not nilpotent-by-finite and whose
growth function has as a majorant a function of the form $c^{\sqrt{n}}$, where $c$ is a
constant greater than $1$?

Here the growth function $\gamma_S(n)$ counts the elements of $G$ that are products of at most
$n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$, where $S$ is a finite generating set of $G$. Nilpotent-by-finite
groups are the virtually nilpotent groups (`Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
      ¬ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ √(n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.9»

modeling_decisions: Finitely generated is expressed by the existence of a finite S with Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ (the same S used for the growth function), rather than a separate Group.FG hypothesis; these are equivalent.

'Nilpotent-by-finite' is rendered as Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent (∃ nilpotent finite-index subgroup). This is equivalent to having a nilpotent normal subgroup with finite quotient, since a finite-index subgroup contains a finite-index normal subgroup and subgroups of nilpotent groups are nilpotent.

The majorant bound is required for all n : ℕ (not just eventually) and for some finite generating set (not every one). Both choices are immaterial up to enlarging c > 1, since γ_S(n) is finite for each n and word metrics of different finite generating sets are bi-Lipschitz. At n = 0 the bound reads 1 ≤ 1.
c is a real constant with 1 < c (strict, as in the source) and c^{√n} is real rpow; the growth function is cast to ℝ for the comparison.
Group G ranges over Type (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files in the repository.

/-!
# Conjecture 9.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated group which is not nilpotent-by-finite and whose
growth function has as a majorant a function of the form $c^{\sqrt{n}}$, where $c$ is a
constant greater than $1$?

Here the growth function of a finitely generated group $G$ with respect to a finite
generating set $S$ is $\gamma_S(n) = |\{g \in G : |g|_S \le n\}|$, the number of elements of
$G$ of word length at most $n$. A group is nilpotent-by-finite if it has a nilpotent normal
subgroup of finite index, i.e. if it is virtually nilpotent. This question is closely related
to Grigorchuk's gap conjecture, see `GapConjecture.gap_conjecture`.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- [On the Gap Conjecture concerning group growth](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6044) by
  *Rostislav Grigorchuk*
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.9»

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated group $G$ which is not nilpotent-by-finite and whose
growth function $\gamma_S$, with respect to a finite generating set $S$, satisfies
$\gamma_S(n) \le c^{\sqrt{n}}$ for all $n$, where $c > 1$ is a constant?

Changing the finite generating set, or only requiring the bound for all large $n$, changes
the question only up to enlarging the constant $c$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
      ¬ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ √(n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.9»

/-!
# Conjecture 9.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated group which is not nilpotent-by-finite and
whose growth function has as a majorant a function of the form $c^{\sqrt{n}}$,
where $c$ is a constant greater than $1$?

Here the growth function of a group $G$ with respect to a finite generating set $S$
is $\gamma_S(n) = |\{g \in G : g \text{ is a product of at most } n
\text{ elements of } S \cup S^{-1}\}|$. A group is nilpotent-by-finite exactly when
it is virtually nilpotent. A negative answer is Grigorchuk's gap conjecture.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- [On the Gap Conjecture concerning group growth](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6044) by
  *Rostislav Grigorchuk*
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.9»

open GromovPolynomialGrowth

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated group which is not nilpotent-by-finite and
whose growth function has as a majorant a function of the form $c^{\sqrt{n}}$,
where $c$ is a constant greater than $1$?

The group is given with a finite generating set $S$, and the majorant condition is
$\gamma_S(n) \le c^{\sqrt{n}}$ for all $n$. Since growth functions for different
finite generating sets differ only by a linear rescaling of $n$, and finitely many
values can be absorbed by enlarging $c$, the choice of $S$ and "for all $n$" versus
"for all large $n$" do not affect the question.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]

    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (S : Set G), S.Finite ∧ Subgroup.closure S = ⊤ ∧
      ¬ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (GrowthFunction S n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ Real.sqrt n := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.9»
